 Shri Laxmi Narayan Soni - Senior Advocate with Shri D
 Advocate for applicant.

Shri Kamal Kumar Tiwari - Govt. Advocate for the resp
 Order

This first bail application under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (equivalent to Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the applicant Mohd. Jakir S/o Mohd.
Siddique Khan for grant of regular bail, who has been arrested on 30.05.2024 in connection with Crime No.190/2024 registered at Police Station M.G. Road, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 474, 120-B, 409 and 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.

entities.text: Police Station M.G. Road, District Indore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
As per prosecution story, the complainant, Harish Shrivastava, made a written complaint dt.
28.05.2024 to police station M.G. Road Indore regarding lodging an FIR against firms namely King Constructions, Green Constructions and Jahanvi Enterprises for preparation and presentation of four forged bills with regard to the work of trenching ground, Indore.
When NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6753 2 MCRC-10009-2025 the said bills were verified by concerned authorities, the same were found forged and fabricated.

Based on the said written compliant,
non-applicant No.1 registered the case against co-accused Mohd. Sajid, Mohd. Siddique, Renu Vadera, Rahul Vadera and present applicant Mohd. Jakir for forging bills of fake work and presented them in the concerned department of the Municipal Corporation and Rs.1,40,40,000/-
got deposited in the bank account of King Construction belongs to the applicant.
3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant has been implicated in the present case falsely.
It is further submitted that the applicant is a 50 years old person.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that in the present case, the applicant has not played any role in the offence.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that co-accused persons namely Murlidhar, Jagidsh Chandra Choukse have already been enlarged on bail by trial Court even after similar allegations.

Counsel for the applicant submits that in another related crime number the Mohd. Jakir vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176833579/
1 accused namely Mohd. Aihatesham Khan and Bilkis Khan were granted anticipatory bail by this Court on 16.10.2024 because Aihatesham Khan has earlier deposited entire amount in another Crime No.171/2024 in compliance of the directions of Hon'ble Apex Court.

entities.text: Mohd. Jakir vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in the same crime number i.e. in 171/2024, accused Jahid Khan has also granted regular bail subject to deposit 50% of the embezzled amount in that crime.
Learned counsel for the applicant, at the end of arguments has also submitted that the applicant is also ready to deposit 50% of the amount received by the applicant in his account.

Co-accused Mohd. Siddique has also been granted bail by this Court vide NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6753 3 MCRC-10009-2025 order dated 07/02/2025 passed in M.Cr.C.No.54014/2024 in the similar circumstances.
Therefore looking to the parity also, the applicant is also entitled to get bail.

4. On the contrary, learned Government Advocate for the State has opposed the prayer by submitting that the persons who have been granted bail by trial Court were only the employees of the Indore Nagar Nigam, whereas the applicant is one of the main accused.
However, he has not disputed the factum of release of similarly situated co-accused Moh. Siddique.
It is also submitted that in the present case, the applicant has received approximately Rs.1,40,40,000/- in his account.
5. I have heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, the fact that the applicant is an old person aged about 50 years and he is ready to deposit 50% of the entire amount as alleged by the prosecution and custody period, without commenting upon the merits of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to allow this application.
Accordingly, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that subject to deposit 50% of the total amount of Rs.1,40,40,000/- i.e.
Rs.70,20,000/- before the trial Court, applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond also in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS,2023.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6753 4 MCRC-10009-2025 8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
9. The disbursement of the aforesaid amount, if deposited by the applicant, shall be subject to final outcome of the trial.
Certified copy as per rules.
